summary: node1 now runs a rootless containerized BusyBox web application as the non-login appsvc account on port 8080. It starts through appsvc’s lingering systemd user manager without an active login session and recovered successfully after a full node reboot.
actions_performed: Created appsvc as unprivileged UID 999 with /usr/sbin/nologin.
Created a minimal root filesystem and isolated the application with user, mount, UTS, IPC, and PID namespaces.
Configured and enabled webapp-container.service under appsvc’s systemd user manager.
Verified HTTP service through node1’s managed IP on port 8080.
Restarted node1 once and verified automatic service and data recovery.

evidence.requirement: Containerized web application runs as unprivileged appsvc on port 8080
evidence.summary: Before and after reboot, the HTTP process runs as host UID 999, maps only to UID 0 inside its private user namespace, has distinct container namespaces and NSpid 1, listens on port 8080, and returns the expected content through $NODE_IP.

evidence.requirement: Service starts at boot while appsvc has no active login session
evidence.summary: Shows the enabled user unit, Linger=yes, an empty Sessions field, active appsvc user manager, and automatically recovered webapp-container.service after reboot.

Healthy pre-restart HTTP and old boot ID 0d49f077-ed5b-479a-b08e-ec4392d89c52 were captured with reboot acknowledgement; node1 returned with changed boot ID 17ce4a5c-5afd-4144-84f4-f81100dd9f90; post-restart proof confirms the user manager, container, listener, and web content recovered.
